correctness.rationale: The final RESULT.md corrects the false displayed equality in the frozen exact witness (line 75): the sign of h is the sign of 1−t(4−3t), not (1−t)−t(4−3t). This restores the factorization (1−t)(1−3t) without changing the claim. Independently eliminating the susceptible variable using pS(1−e^(−βI))=δI gives the stated continuous, strictly increasing r(I), with range (r_c,∞); no positive equilibrium occurs at equality. The log-ratio L has strictly decreasing derivative when c>w and stays bounded. Hence h(I)/I strictly increases for w<1, from b(1−w)−κ to b(1−w); for w=1 the ratio in L directly gives the negative or identically zero case. Substitution at t=1/3 gives the witness, and independent differentiation gives the repaired text's Jacobian and positive Schur margins for 1<log 3<2. A separate numerical calculation from the original map gave an equilibrium residual at roundoff and margins 0.40957, 0.11508, 3.06578; the exact proof, not this check, establishes the result. The frozen verification notes and checker use the correct polynomial and need no change.
residual_risks: Stability is proved only locally for the explicit branch near its crossing; the all-parameter comparison makes no attractor or trajectory claim.

value.rationale: A complete partition in reproductive capacity answers when the direction of an equilibrium population difference changes, not merely when the effect can occur. The example establishes that the direction changes even on a locally attracting branch outside both earlier sufficient restrictions. The result is valuable as a sharp comparison for this model, not as a claim about observed trajectories.
residual_risks: No general stability or empirical claim accompanies the sign classification.
